answers.question: I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?
answers.answer:
No, not yet, on both counts. Going to 40 miles would more than triple last week's 12 miles in one step, and the legs need a few more easy weeks before anything that stresses them. Speedwork can start after about two more weeks of easy runs that feel normal, beginning with short strides before any faster reps.

What comes next for you: a 10K in late November, another marathon, or a break from racing for a while? Tell me the race and its date, and I will build the plan from there.

new.analysis:
## What happened last week
Last week was followed exactly. The three easy runs were the planned 3, 4 and 5 miles, and the rest days were taken as scheduled. Pain stayed at 0 out of 10 and sleep averaged 7.5 hours, so nothing in the week points to a problem.

## Easy pace is coming back too fast
Your easy pace went from 10:49 on Wednesday to 9:51 on Sunday, while heart rate climbed from 128 to 139. The Sunday pace matches what you ran before the race. A pace that returns this fast often means the legs feel good, not that the damage from 26 miles has fully cleared, so heart rate is the limit for now.

## What the race tells us
The race finished at about 3:50 on your watch, five minutes slower than the target. The first 20 miles ran faster than the 8:35 per mile that a 3:45 needs, and the last 6 miles slowed sharply.

| Segment | Pace per mile |
| --- | --- |
| Miles 1 to 20 | 8:25 to 8:40 |
| Miles 21 to 26 | 9:25 to 9:31 |
| Pace needed for 3:45 | 8:35 |

The early pace was too quick for the target, so the fade after mile 20 was the price. The next marathon needs a slower start and more practice holding marathon pace in the long runs.

## Why this week is still easy
The week of Oct 26 is still recovery, and the legs need easy running before any sharper work. Four short runs, about 18 miles, step up gently from last week's 12 miles without asking much of the legs. Rest days between runs let the legs absorb the work.
